# lme4 formula
![](images/formula.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

When using the `formula=` parameter of the `maaslin3()` function the formula needs to be specified in `lme4` specification.

The following terms can be included in a lme4 formula:

- Fixed effects
- Random effects
- Interaction terms
- Others

The `lme4` specification was originally created for the [`lme4` R package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lme4/index.html) which stands for "Liner Mixed Effect Models using 'Eigen' and S4".

## Our formula

The formula we specify to `maaslin3()` is a string that contains our formula.
The string contains the column names from `metadata` that we want to use.

Below is the formula that we specified:

`'~ Soil + Reads + (1|Plate)`

### ~

The first feature of note is the `~` operator.
This separates the responses and the fixed and random effects

### Fixed and random effects

To the right of the `~` operator are the fixed effects and random effects.

Fixed effects are specified as normal strings.
Our fixed effects are `"Soil + Reads"`.

More information is in the [Fixed effects page](/maaslin3/fixed_effects.qmd).

Random effects are specified as strings within brackets that includes a pipe symbol (`(|)`)
We've set `Plate` as a random effect with: `"(1|Plate)"`.

More information is in the [Random effects page](/maaslin3/random_effects.qmd)

### Responses

The response variable is the variable that we’re testing for associations against our metadata. e.g. Pseudomonas abundance. 
In standard regression, the response variable is written to the left of the `~`. 
In MaAsLin3, we usually leave the left-hand side empty because it automatically models each feature (Genus in our analysis) in the abundance table as a response variable, separately.
